function: Learned active user detection (Transformer, variable pilot length) and diffusion-model joint channel estimation and data detection with a learned channel-prior score network, for massive random access (p. 1-3, 7).
system: Narrowband uplink grant-free random access: BS with 8x8 UPA (144 antennas in one test), K=128 single-antenna users, activity probability 0.1, 4QAM, 3.5 GHz; no RIS (p. 3, 10-11).
method: Heterogeneous-Transformer AUD with pilot-length adaptive module, binary cross-entropy (supervised); NCSN++ score network by denoising score matching; predictor-corrector reverse-diffusion sampling with LMMSE initialization (p. 5-9).
data_channel: 3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS channels at 3.5 GHz generated with QuaDRiGa: 64,000 samples for AUD, 160,000 for the score network; i.i.d. Rayleigh also used (p. 11).
test_conditions: AUD trained at M=64, pilot lengths 10-28; tested also at M=144 and activity probability 0.06-0.2. CE and DD tested over SNR, pilot length, data length (p. 11-14).
baselines: AUD: AMP and OMP. JCEDD non-learned: LS-CE, ZF, OAMP, iterative LMMSE-CE & OAMP-DD; learned: iterative Langevin CE & DD [33]; ablations without PLAM or SCM (p. 11).
metrics: Activity error probability (AEP), false-alarm versus missed-detection probability, NMSE, BER; computation latency per batch or realization (p. 11-15).
complexity: Tab. 1 gives complexity orders of Algorithm 2, e.g. O(L^2 M + Ka^2 M + Ka Fnet) per channel score; measured latency 1.70-2.32 s per realization (p. 9, 14).
q1_support: p. 11: "We consider a 3GPP-compliant channel model [39] generated using Quadriga [49], simulating the 3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS scenario".
q2_support: p. 12: "testing the model trained with M = 64 antennas on the channels with M = 144 antennas". Another number of antennas than in training; Fig. 8 also varies the activity probability.
q3_support: p. 11: "Iter Langevin CE & DD: Conduct iterative CE and DD using ALD [33]" (earlier learned score-based method). Non-learned Pilot LS-CE & ZF-DD, Iter LMMSE-CE & OAMP-DD and, for AUD, AMP and OMP; compared on NMSE, BER (Fig. 10, p. 12-13) and AEP.
q4_support: p. 9: "The complexity analysis of Algorithm 2 is detailed in Tab. 1", with orders such as O(L2 M+Ka2 M+Ka Fnet); p. 14: "we present the average computation latency for one single realization" (Tab. 2).
q5_support: p. 11: "A total of 64,000 channel samples are generated using Quadriga". Self-generated data from a third-party simulator; no code or data link, public dataset or measurement is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: The PDF is arXiv v3 (6 Feb 2026) of 'Generative Diffusion Model Driven Massive Random Access in Massive MIMO Systems'; it prints no journal DOI (only the arXiv DOI in the metadata), so the DOI-title match and equality with the published text cannot be checked. Area 2 chosen because the learned network of the joint estimation and detection is the channel prior (the data prior is closed form, p. 7-9) and CE comes first; BER for detection (area 1) is reported with equal weight in Figs. 10-15, so the reviewer may confirm. Active user detection acts on received pilots (physical layer), not on access control, and CE and DD are physical layer anyway. q3 counts the iterative Langevin method [33] as the earlier learned joint CE and DD design; AUD is compared only with AMP, OMP and own variants.
